patch.value: GH-1777: pm package list prints the bundled catalog instead of the installed packages, and the four package listings take different --fields contracts

GH-1777 (filed 2026-11-24 from a project with two npm-installed packages). pm package list, pm packages list and pm extension list are Commander aliases of pm package catalog (alias contract owner pm-ya7x55), so the most natural question an agent asks, which packages does this tracker have, prints the 13 bundled first-party packages (11,976 B toon on this repo) with installed=false rows and none of the packages actually installed. The installed set is spread across explore (5,991 B), manage (6,018 B, each row embeds the full contributions JSON and it is the only listing with update metadata) and inventory (526 B, static, one line per package). catalog accepts --fields; manage, explore and inventory refuse it with unknown_option. pm extensions list (plural) is refused as an unknown command and the did-you-mean suggests package, package activate, package adopt, none of which lists anything. Reproduced on 2026.11.25 in this repo. The report's hub ran seven-week-old extensions because only manage --json exposes update_available. pm-fr6u17 (closed, GH-937) fixed alias rows inside the catalog, not which listing list names. Duplicate check: searched package list installed catalog inventory, extension list did you mean, package manage fields; no open owner.

pm package list (and pm packages list, pm extension list) lists the packages installed in the selected scope, and pm package catalog keeps listing the bundled catalog; the alias contract, help, completion and contracts agree; Each package listing (list/inventory, explore, manage, catalog) accepts the same --fields contract and refuses an unknown field with the allowed values; pm package manage rows leave the embedded contributions map out unless requested with --fields, because pm package describe maps them; pm extensions list suggests pm package list
An agent that runs pm package list sees exactly the installed packages in a few hundred bytes, and every listing answers --fields the same way

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Implementation: pm package list, pm packages list and pm extension list are now aliases of pm package inventory (Commander alias moved off catalog; alias contracts owner pm-gh1777, extension list targets package inventory because the deprecated extension vocabulary has no live-contract inventory row); catalog keeps the bundled catalog. Inventory rows gain update (last observed newer version for the installed version) and the result gains updates_available. One --fields contract (parseListingFields/projectListingRows, published with the inventory reader so the CLI stays on the SDK export closure) on list, explore, manage and catalog; unknown keys are refused as 'must be one of a|b|c', which recovery turns into allowed_values. Default explore/manage rows drop the embedded contributions map (--fields ...,contributions restores it). pm extensions list now suggests package list with an executable --help retry: a singular/plural slip of a noun that is neither a command nor an alias resolves through the alias contracts, then follows typed operands. Measured on this repo: package list 574 B (was 11,976 B, the catalog); explore 5,991 to 3,837 B; manage 6,018 to 3,864 B. Static fast path covers list. Gates: grammar, flag contracts, contracts fixture, completion, SDK surface (two additive inventory type changes acknowledged), static chain green.

value.negative_control: tests/unit/cli/static-extension-inventory.spec.ts runs pm package list and expects the installed inventory rows with the observed update column and the shared --fields refusal; on 2026.11.25 pm package list resolves to the bundled catalog (13 rows, installed=false, no installed packages) and --fields on inventory is refused as unknown_option; tests/unit/cli/canonical-command-recovery.spec.ts pins pm extensions list suggesting package list

patch.value: pm package list, pm packages list and pm extension list are now aliases of the static inventory (installed packages in the selected scope, no extension code activated), with an update column from the last pm package manage observation and an updates_available count; pm package catalog keeps the bundled catalog. list, explore, manage and catalog share one --fields contract on the CLI and in the MCP/SDK explore and manage action schemas; an unknown key is refused with the listing's whole domain. Default explore and manage rows leave out the embedded contributions map. pm extensions list now suggests package list with an executable help retry, through a new singular/plural noun step that leaves real commands and aliases to the existing ranking. Alias contracts, grammar rows, flag contracts, help, completion, the static fast path, the dogfood script and the contracts fixture agree.

On this repo pm package list prints the 4 installed packages in 574 B (was 11,976 B of catalog); explore and manage rows dropped from about 6.0 KB to 3.8 KB; --fields works on all four listings and refuses unknown keys with the domain; pm extensions list suggests package list
pm package list lists the installed packages, and every package listing takes one --fields contract

value.api: pm package list / pm packages list / pm extension list, pm package explore and manage rows, and the SDK StaticExtensionInventoryEntry/StaticExtensionInventoryResult types
value.before: pm package list was an alias of pm package catalog and returned the bundled catalog (details.packages); explore and manage rows embedded the full contributions map; inventory rows had no update column
value.after: pm package list is an alias of pm package inventory and returns the installed packages of the selected scope (extensions[] with an update column, plus updates_available); pm package catalog returns the bundled catalog; explore and manage rows leave contributions out unless --fields asks for it; list, explore, manage and catalog share one --fields contract
value.migrate: Scripts that read the bundled catalog from pm package list switch to pm package catalog (same rows and --fields); readers of contributions in explore or manage rows pass --fields with contributions, or use pm package describe

value.text: Review round 1 fixes on the listing side: pm package --global list (scope switch before the verb) now stays on the static no-activation path (Codex P1); explore/manage validate --fields at action admission, before adoption, remote checks or observation writes (Codex P2); pm extension explore/manage --fields keep their subcommand route instead of the legacy root rewrite (Codex P2); catalog --fields uses the shared parser, so its refusal carries the whole catalog domain as allowed_values / legal_domain, keeping its curated example (Codex P2, Greptile); the shared fields tool metadata names package row keys and adds a package example (Codex P3); the inflected did-you-mean follows operands with the bootstrap scanner, so pm extensions --json list and --author <value> forms resolve to package list (Codex P3); pm extension list --help now shows the inventory help bundle (CodeRabbit; the cause was a missing extension inventory help entry, not the positional action table).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review round 2 listing fixes: the static detector skips root switches and valued root options before the verb (pm package --offline list, --ref v1 list) without reading a value as the verb; bootstrap resolves the package leaf past a scope switch so repeated --fields accumulate (pm package --project list --fields a --fields b); flat MCP/SDK fields now hoist on the root package action, so package-explore/manage/catalog honor a flat fields parameter; pm package list refuses row-shaping read-output controls with read_output_surface_unsupported instead of silently ignoring them (--output-format and --output-budget unbounded still apply); listing --fields refusals carry code invalid_argument_value and recovery.allowed_values with the whole domain for SDK and MCP callers.

value.text: Review round 3 listing fixes: one shared lifecycle verb parser (resolveLifecycleVerb in the SDK bootstrap) now serves static selection, bootstrap leaf resolution and plural-noun recovery, so pm --no-changed-fields package list and pm package --offline list stay static (noun found with the host-option grammar), pm package --offline list x --fields=a --fields=b accumulates, and pm extensions --ref v1 list suggests package list. SDK/MCP dispatch of the static listing is recorded as scope on the follow-up listing item.

value.text: Review round 9 (Codex: 0 P1, 5 P2, 1 P3). Fixed: pm package list applies the tracker's output.default_format (read from settings.json without the scaffolding settings reader), which the catalog alias honored on main; the terminator before the command is found by walking host options with their arity (removeLeadingCommandTerminator in the SDK bootstrap), so pm --pm-path -- --json -- package list stays static; COMMANDS.md says human text bounds a long field domain and --json carries all of it. Re-reported and already owned: SDK/MCP static listing dispatch (pm-q5iao5) and npm install-resolution provenance (pm-4qq9jy). Not changed, with reason: a FIFO planted at the observation lock path would block core acquireLock metadata reads for every lock in the tracker, not only this one; that is a core lock-primitive concern outside this PR.

value.text: Codex review round 23 on PR #1782 (P2, fixed): the legacy-action rewrite kept a pm extension invocation on its subcommand route whenever any argv token looked like a fields projection, including a host flag value (pm --author fields extension install a b took the variadic installer instead of the single-target action route). The bypass now applies only to the explore and manage listings, and only to tokens after the action up to a terminator.

value.text: Codex review round 24 on PR #1782, fixed: the bootstrap lifecycle-leaf scan accepted any operand after root options as the subcommand, so pm package --install ./demo --dry_run took ./demo as the leaf, lost the root flag table and left --dry_run unnormalized (main normalized it); a token found only after root options now counts as the leaf when it names a lifecycle subcommand. The pm package list read-output refusal names the first refused control in its structured flag, never a valid --fields projection. COMMANDS.md says the JSON field domain is complete within the default diagnostic budget and that the SDK error context always holds all of it.
